findings: CVE-2026-56767 is PUBLISHED, GitHub advisory GHSA-44p3-ph5c-h5h3 has withdrawn_at=null, and the repository/advisory mechanism and 0.0.42 fix are confirmed.

The primary chose 7e225829 because it first wrote the surviving Sequelize query forms, but its parent already exposed the same global recordings through readFiles, deleteFile, and getRecordingByFileName. That commit merely changed storage representation and is barred by the protocol's move/refactor rule.

The corrected first-write commit 0ee54bf1f0912b5ac317516ba5c7668f9b963e96 created storage.ts and globally exposed recordings and runs without authentication or ownership checks; user authentication arrived later, and 5d8cc4a091929e661a14b63e7037bffab0aa55e5 narrowed these routes to signed-in users without adding per-user ownership.
The corrected BIC remains human-authored with no AI marker, so the causal verdict remains NOT_AI even though the primary introducer and parent fields require correction.

corrected_fields.flaw_origin: The missing object-level authorization was first written by 0ee54bf1f0912b5ac317516ba5c7668f9b963e96 when it created server/src/routes/storage.ts with global recording/run listing, attacker-selected deletion, retrieval, and execution and no authentication or owner predicate. Authentication was added later without ownership scoping; 7e225829 only migrated the already-vulnerable operations from shared files to unscoped Robot/Run queries.
